user_consequence: A player (or coach viewing a teammate) on /golf/dashboard/stats sees the single 'Overview' sub-nav tab rendered as the CURRENT page (green text, gliding underline, aria-current="page"), even though clicking it navigates AWAY to a completely different route (/golf/dashboard/coachhelm). user_consequence: A player or coach who switches the round-scope picker (or the player itself, for a coach browsing the roster) more than once before the first request finishes can end up looking at stats for the WRONG scope — the screen silently shows stale data for a round/player they already navigated away from, with no indication anything is wrong.
mechanism: `loadAll` (StatsSpineStage.tsx:122-178) carries no request generation counter, AbortSignal, or 'am I still current' guard. It is invoked from a `useEffect` keyed on [playerId, scopeRoundId] (line 180-182) and again directly from onClick retry handlers (lines 361,420,503,529). If two invocations overlap (e.g. selecting round A then quickly round B before A's `getPlayerStatsDashboardBundle` resolves), JS resolves promises in COMPLETION order, not call order; whichever call's `.then`/`finally` executes last unconditionally calls every setState (setDetailedStats, setStandingRows, etc., lines 129-177) with no check that its own `id`/`roundId` still matches the current `scopeRoundId`/`playerId` state. The slower, older request can overwrite the newer, correct one. The underlying server action (`stats-dashboard.ts`) also accepts no AbortSignal/generation param, so there is no cancellation path at any layer.
expected: Per C02/T03: reject/discard a request whose scope no longer matches the current selection when it resolves out of order.
actual: No generation/cancellation guard exists in `loadAll` or its call sites.
proposed_fix: Add a request-generation ref (increment on every loadAll call; capture at call time; only apply setState if the captured generation === current ref) — the same pattern the round-options effect at lines 186-207 already correctly uses via its `cancelled` closure flag. Reuse that exact idiom in `loadAll` rather than inventing a new mechanism.

user_consequence: Retrying a single failed optional section (the putting/approach leak maps) throws away the entire visible Stats page — spine, bento, every drill — and replaces it with a full-page skeleton for the duration of refetching all 8 reads, even though only one of those 8 reads failed. Switching the round-scope picker does the same full-page blank-out even though most of the bundle (standing, trends, patterns) is cross-round and unaffected by the switch.

Do the same for the round-scope switch: keep detailedStats/spray (the only two reads that actually depend on `roundId`) behind their own scoped-loading flag rather than the page-wide `loading`.
performance_check: Refetches 8 server reads (up to a combined ~15s worst-case timeout budget per settleWithin calls in stats-dashboard.ts:89-96) to retry 1.

user_consequence: A player who decides to tap the calendar's single 'Respond' primary action cannot see, at the moment of deciding, which event it will open — the button carries no event title/date. If a background realtime notification (any golf_events row change on the team, not necessarily this event) lands and triggers router.refresh()+refetchVisibleRange() between the player's decision to tap and the actual pointerup, React will have already swapped the onClick handler to point at whatever event is now 'most imminent un-RSVP'd' before the click fires — so the player can open, and RSVP to, a different event than the one they meant to respond to, with no on-screen warning that the target changed.
mechanism: FairwayCalendar.tsx's `mostImminentUnrsvpd` (a useMemo over `events`/`serverNow`/`userRsvpStatuses`) feeds `handlePrimaryAction` (a useCallback that closes over it) which is passed to FairwayCalendarHero as `onPrimaryAction`. `events` itself is `useCalendarRangeEvents(...).events`, which is intentionally live-updated by the realtime channel's `onRealtimeEvent: () => router.refresh()` and by every `postgres_changes` event on `golf_events` for the team (use-calendar-range-events.ts:502-545) — not scoped to the specific event being displayed. Because React always uses the onClick prop current at click time, not the one visible when the user last read the label, any re-render between decision and tap silently retargets the button. FairwayCalendarHero.tsx never renders the target event's title/date next to the 'Respond' label (only the isCoach ? 'New event' : 'Respond' static string), so there is no way for the player to notice, even after the fact, that the button just changed meaning.
expected: Section 7's Calendar interaction contract: 'Named event-bound RSVP... Reject the design when... a global Respond button silently changes target.'
actual: Respond is bound to a named event id at click time (not a truly global button), but the id it is bound to can change between the last paint the user saw and the actual click, and the button never displays which event it targets.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: render the target event's title/date inline on or beside the primary action ('Respond to Practice — Thu 4:00 PM') so a retarget is visible before the tap; and/or freeze `mostImminentUnrsvpd` for the duration of a user gesture (e.g. snapshot on pointerdown, or debounce the realtime-triggered recompute while a press is in flight) so a background refresh cannot change the committed target mid-gesture. Reuse the existing FairwayCalendarHero composition and A03 Button/typography tokens — no new primitive.

user_consequence: A WKWebView URL that happens to contain the substring "/golf/" anywhere (not anchored to path start, no origin/host check) is treated as a legitimate in-app page and the native safety net that returns the user to the sign-in screen never fires. Conversely a genuine in-app URL that omits that exact substring (e.g. the bare "/golf" root before its server redirect resolves) can misfire the callback, which reloads the WKWebView with a full hardcoded document navigation to https://www.helmsportslabs.com/golf/login, discarding all SPA state including any unsaved round/session data with no confirmation.

When neither matches, SceneDelegate's onNavigateAway closure fires a hardcoded webView.load(URLRequest(url: "https://www.helmsportslabs.com/golf/login")) - a full document reload, not an SPA route change.
expected: Navigation classification should anchor on the app's actual origin/host and path prefix (e.g. URL host equals the deployed app host AND path starts with /golf/), not a bare substring match anywhere in the URL string; a false classification either way should not cause a silent security bypass or an undiscovered destructive reload of in-progress work.
actual: Classification is two unanchored String.contains calls with no host/origin check at all.
proposed_fix: A01 (native shell owner) anchors the classifier on URL.host matching the deployed app host and URL.path having the /golf/ (or /about, /privacy, /terms) prefix, using URLComponents rather than raw string containment. A08 requests this as a shared contract (C05 viewport/native boundary) since the failure mode intersects auth/session integrity.

user_consequence: A player or coach sees one number on the Team/Operations rail item, the mobile bottom-nav 5th column, and the More sheet row for it, with no way to tell from the number whether it means an unread announcement, a pending task, or an unseen travel itinerary -- three different objects with three different clearing actions on three different screens. Opening the destination the badge points at does not necessarily clear the count the user saw, because the number was never about that one destination.

Upstream, buildPlayerRailSections composes the player's single 'Team' rail item's badge as announcements+tasks+travel summed (nav-registry.ts:433), and MoreNavSheet's OverflowRow renders only the one combined integer (no sub-breakdown) next to the row label.

user_consequence: A transient read failure on the unified notifications-unread count or the CoachHelm alert count makes the bell badge and the CoachHelm rail badge drop to a confident zero, indistinguishable from 'nothing to see' -- exactly the failure mode the file's own comments say the messages/announcements/tasks counts were fixed to avoid.

user_consequence: A player who opens the Announcements page and reads every posted announcement still carries an unread-looking badge (feeding the combined Team count, A09-001) for up to 24 hours after publish, because reading the page never clears it. The badge's 'unread' semantics for non-acknowledgement-required announcements are pure time-decay, not read state.
mechanism: getPlayerNotificationCountsImpl counts a non-ack-required announcement as unread whenever `Date.now() - published_at < 24h`, with zero reference to lastSeenAt or any per-player read marker (player-notifications.ts:212-222). markAnnouncementsSeen (the only function that advances the state row this count could reference) is called from exactly one place in the whole app -- the login/unseen-announcements modal (NewAnnouncementsModalWrapper.tsx:49) -- never from the actual Announcements route (src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/announcements/page.tsx), which fetches and renders the list but never touches badges.refetch() or markAnnouncementsSeen.

user_consequence: A player mid round-entry (or any active task) who receives a push notification gets a native iOS banner + sound (system-presented while the app is open) AND an in-app toast for the exact same event, plus a haptic buzz -- two competing presentations and a haptic for one event, which is the precise double-notification failure the attention policy is meant to prevent, and a real interruption risk during active data entry.
mechanism: capacitor.config.ts sets PushNotifications.presentationOptions to ['badge','sound','alert'], which (per the Capacitor push-notifications plugin) tells iOS to present the system alert+sound even while the WebView is foregrounded. Independently, initPushListeners' 'pushNotificationReceived' handler (push-registration.ts) fires fwHaptic('light') and dispatches PUSH_RECEIVED_EVENT; CapacitorProvider.tsx's onReceived listener turns that into a fairwayToast(...) in-app banner. Nothing suppresses the native alert when the in-app toast is about to render the same content, and nothing suppresses the toast/haptic when the app is in the foreground and the system will already show its own alert.
expected: One event produces exactly one presentation (native banner when backgrounded, one in-app affordance when foregrounded) plus at most one haptic, per Section 9.4's 'A button, handler and success toast cannot independently vibrate for the same event' and the work order's explicit double-notification requirement.
actual: presentationOptions always includes 'alert'+'sound' (foreground included) while the app additionally renders its own toast+haptic for the identical received event -- two banners, one haptic, every foreground push.
proposed_fix: Either drop 'alert'/'sound' from presentationOptions when the app can detect it is foregrounded (Capacitor's plugin does not expose a runtime per-notification override, so this likely means moving to a foreground-only in-app presentation and only allowing the system to show 'alert' while backgrounded, which needs an app-state check before deciding whether to also show the in-app toast), or drop the in-app toast/haptic entirely for foreground pushes and rely solely on the system presentation. Requires an explicit product decision on which channel wins in the foreground case -- flagged as an open question below.

user_consequence: With HELM_CUSTOMER_EMAIL_ENABLED off (the recorded current owner default), a player whose coach creates a new qualifier or assigns them a development plan receives literally zero signal of it -- no email (suppressed by the gate), no push, no bell/More entry, and no badge increment anywhere in GolfNavBadgeCounts. The only way to discover either event is to manually browse to Qualifiers or My Development. Task assignment is partially covered (the pendingTasks badge does increment via the real golf_task_assignments row) but still produces no push/bell signal, only a silent count bump.
mechanism: notifyQualifierCreated (called from golf.ts:4220) and notifyDevPlanAssigned (called from development.ts:339) both route exclusively through sendEmailNotificationDirect, which is now suppressed by gateCustomerEmail (outbound-gate.ts) -- correctly, per the recorded owner decision. Neither call site independently inserts a row into the generic `notifications` table (the one the unified bell/dispatch.ts/task-reminders.ts pipeline reads) nor increments any field in GolfNavBadgeCounts, unlike task-reminders.ts, which writes its own `notifications` row in addition to its (also gated) email.

user_consequence: A user taps a push notification, is deep-linked straight to the exact object it named, clearly sees it -- and the corresponding bell badge count does not go down. The notification stays 'unread' until the user separately opens the bell panel and taps (or long-presses mark-all-read on) the same item again, which most users will never do, so the badge overcounts indefinitely relative to what the user has actually seen.

Is the target marked read before the applicable visibility rule says it was seen?' -- a push tap that lands the user on the named object should mark that notification read.

user_consequence: Tapping 'Download' on a coach/player document (PDF, image, or the PDFViewer/ImagePreview toolbar) does not reliably download the file in place inside the native app; depending on the runtime branch, it may silently do nothing, or hand off to the external Safari app for what the user expects to be an in-app action.

user_consequence: The CoachHelm player-home prediction sentence reads 'Predicted to shoot 74.2 at 78% confidence.' A reasonable reader takes that as '78% chance of shooting exactly/close to 74.2 strokes.' The system does not compute that quantity.
mechanism: `buildPredictionVerdict` (buildPlayerHomeViewModel.ts:144-159) concatenates the point estimate and the confidence percent into one sentence with no distinguishing clause. The confidence value it formats (`data.prediction.calibratedConfidence ?? data.prediction.confidence`, PlayerCoachHelmHome.tsx:290) traces to `performance-predictor.ts`'s `calculateConfidenceInterval` (lines 396-421), which sets a fixed 0.6/0.7/0.8 tier from the player's score stdDev — an 80%-style confidence-INTERVAL width, not a point-probability — and is then optionally recalibrated by `confidence-calibrator.ts`'s bucket lookup, which measures `was_accurate` = `direction==='accurate' || withinInterval` (outcome-validator.ts:19-55,487) against actual outcomes. So the number genuinely means '~78% of past predictions in this confidence tier had the true score within/near the stated range' — a defensible, empirically calibrated interval-hit-rate — but the UI sentence structure implies it is the probability of the single displayed point value.
expected: Per the work order: 'Do not display a percent as likelihood of a score unless that is its supported interpretation.'
actual: Sentence structure attaches the % directly to the point estimate with no interval/range framing.
proposed_fix: Either surface the actual predicted range (predictedRangeLow/High already computed by performance-predictor.ts:212,238 and persisted at line 507-508) alongside the confidence (e.g. 'Predicted 72-77 strokes (78% of similar predictions land in this range)'), or reword to 'this type of prediction has been accurate ~78% of the time' — an interval/track-record framing instead of a point-probability framing. Not a code defect in the calibration engine itself, which is real (Brier score + ECE tracked, DB-persisted, nightly cron) — the gap is purely in the display sentence.

user_consequence: The Stats spine's Fairways/Greens/Putts rows sit next to a single 'Rounds' count, implying all four numbers share that sample size. They don't — each is computed over a different, unstated denominator — so a player cannot tell how many actual data points back the Fairways% versus the Putts/round figure.
mechanism: `buildLedger` (buildStatsViewModel.ts:149-168) emits exactly 4 rows: Rounds (roundsPlayed), Fairways (fairwayPct), Greens (girPct), Putts/rd (puttsPerRound) — with no per-row sample/denominator field in `SpineLedgerRow`. The canonical calculator computes each over a DIFFERENT population: `fairwayPercentage = safePercent(fairwaysHit, fairwayOpportunities)` (golf-stats-calculator-shots.ts:2617) excludes par-3 holes from the denominator; `girPercentage = safePercent(girTotal, girOpportunities)` (line 2636) uses its own opportunity count; puttsPerRound divides by a separate holes-with-recorded-putts denominator (comment at line 1860-1870). None of `fairwayOpportunities`/`girOpportunities`/the putts denominator, nor a timestamp/calc-version, is threaded from `GolfStats` into `LedgerInput`/`SpineLedgerRow`, so the UI cannot express 'Fairways: 61% (n=142 attempts)' distinctly from 'Rounds: 18' the way `PlayerStandingRow.team_n` already does for the team-average comparison (stats-leak-maps-types.ts:64) — that field similarly isn't rendered anywhere in the Spine/Bento/Standing views I read.
expected: Per C07: sample/completeness should be carryable per metric, not implied by an adjacent, differently-scoped count.
actual: One shared 'Rounds' figure is the only sample-size context for four differently-denominated metrics; team_n exists on standing rows but is never rendered.
proposed_fix: Thread `fairwayOpportunities`/`girOpportunities` (already computed, just not exported through LedgerInput) into SpineLedgerRow as an optional secondary caption, and render `team_n` in the Standing drill/track where a team comparison is shown. This is additive (new optional fields), not a rewrite of the calculator.
owner_lane: A06 (adapter), A10 (independent semantics review per boundary)

user_consequence: If an event is cancelled, rescheduled, or has its RSVP deadline changed by a coach (or by a realtime-triggered refresh) WHILE a player already has that event's detail drawer open, the drawer keeps showing the stale pre-change state: RSVP buttons stay live and unlocked for what is now a cancelled event or a passed deadline. Tapping 'Going'/'Maybe'/'Decline' still submits — the write is correctly rejected server-side (RSVPLockedError) and surfaces as an error string via `rsvpLockMessage`, so no wrong data is persisted, but the player experiences a confusing 'looked fine, then errored' interaction instead of the drawer proactively showing the new locked/cancelled state. The same staleness applies to a coach's edit editor: `editorEvent` is a point-in-time snapshot.
mechanism: FairwayCalendar.tsx holds `drawerEvent`/`editorEvent` as component state, set exactly once in `openDrawerForEvent(event)` / `openEdit(ev)` and cleared only when the sheet closes (drawerEvent additionally cleared via a 240ms setTimeout after close). No effect re-syncs either from the live, realtime-updated `events` array (the same array `mostImminentUnrsvpd` and the day-strip/agenda/month bodies all read from) while the sheet is open. `FairwayEventDetailDrawer`'s lock computation (`isCancelled`, `hasStarted`, `deadlinePassed`, `rsvpLocked`) is derived entirely from the `event` prop it was handed, so it is only ever as fresh as the moment the drawer opened. The same snapshot problem applies to `FairwayEventEditor`'s recurring edit-scope math: `editRecurringEvent`'s `originalStartDate` (used to bound the 'thisAndFuture' scope's row filter, src/app/golf/actions/recurring-events.ts:1227) is `editorEvent.start_date` captured at open time — if a concurrent edit has already moved that occurrence's date by the time the coach saves, the 'future' boundary is computed from a stale anchor date.
expected: Section 9.2's mutation truth table + Section 6 A07 order: 'Check deadlines/locks, cancelation, occurrence edits and permission changes while details are open.'
actual: The drawer/editor never observes a change to the entity it is displaying once open; only the eventual write attempt discovers the new server truth.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: derive `drawerEvent`/`editorEvent` by id-lookup into the live `events` array on every render (`events.find(e => e.id === openId) ?? lastKnownSnapshot`) instead of freezing the object at open time, so a cancellation/reschedule while the sheet is open is reflected live; when the live lookup returns null (hard-deleted while open), show an explicit 'This event was removed' state rather than silently keeping the stale copy. For the recurring edit-scope case, re-derive `originalStartDate` from the live event at submit time rather than at editor-open time.

user_consequence: Navigating (Agenda/Week/Month) to a date range the client hasn't fetched yet can show 'No upcoming events' / 'Nothing upcoming — check back when your coach adds events' at the exact same moment a 'Loading events for this date range…' banner sits above it — the confirmed-empty message and the still-loading message render together, so the user cannot tell whether the calendar is actually empty there or simply hasn't finished asking yet.
mechanism: `FairwayCalendar` renders `isLoadingRange`/`rangeError` only as an inline banner (FairwayCalendar.tsx:1038-1062) directly above the body, but the body components themselves (`FairwayAgendaView`, and by the same pattern `FairwayMonthGrid`) never receive `isLoadingRange` as a prop — their honest-empty branch is gated purely on `totalEvents === 0` (FairwayAgendaView.tsx:236-257 for range mode, :260-285 for day mode), computed from whatever `events` the range hook currently holds. Per `useCalendarRangeEvents` (use-calendar-range-events.ts:336-479), a not-yet-covered range genuinely has zero matching rows in `eventVersions` until its fetch resolves, so the empty state renders immediately and only clears (or doesn't) once the fetch lands — 'zero events' and 'haven't asked yet' are indistinguishable to the body while `isLoadingRange` is true.
expected: Section 9.1: 'New scope without matching result → Stable controls; dependent-region placeholder' and Section 7 Calendar reject-condition: 'empty equals unqueried.'
actual: The honest-empty state and the in-flight loading banner can both be on screen at once for the same navigation, with the empty state written in confirmed-empty language ('Check back when your coach adds events').
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: thread `isLoadingRange` into `FairwayAgendaView`/`FairwayMonthGrid` and render a neutral loading placeholder (skeleton rows, or simply suppress the EmptyState copy) instead of the confirmed-empty state while the exact visible range is still being fetched. Keep the existing banner and the existing beneficial streaming/error handling unchanged — this is additive gating, not a replacement.

user_consequence: On a multi-day event (a tournament, a multi-day trip), the week's day-strip shows a density dot only under the FIRST day of the event; every subsequent day the event actually runs shows no dot and its accessible label reads '— no events', even though the Month grid and the Agenda list directly below correctly show the same event live on those days. A player or coach scanning the day-strip for 'what's happening this week' undercounts multi-day commitments exactly on the days that matter (day 2+ of a tournament).
mechanism: `FairwayDayStrip`'s density-dot bucketing keys events by `zonedDayKey(ev.start_date || ev.start_time, teamTimezone)` — the event's START instant only (FairwayDayStrip.tsx:110-121) — while every other calendar surface in this same file family (`FairwayMonthGrid.tsx:151`, `FairwayAgendaView.tsx:89,126`) explicitly uses `eventDaySpan` from `src/lib/calendar/timezone.ts`, whose own doc comment (timezone.ts:191-208) documents that reading only the start day is precisely the bug class already found and fixed on production ('#1493/#1494/#1495/#1496... all 14 multi-day events... invisible after their first day'). The day-strip is the one caller in this component family that was never updated to the eventDaySpan convention.
expected: eventRunsOnDay/eventDaySpan is the canonical, already-battle-tested rule for 'does this event occupy this calendar day' used consistently by Month and Agenda.
actual: FairwayDayStrip computes day membership independently via start-day-only bucketing, silently disagreeing with the body it sits directly above.
proposed_fix: SOURCE fix, low risk: replace `zonedDayKey`-based bucketing in `eventsByDay` with a pass that calls `eventRunsOnDay(ev, teamTimezone, dayKey)` (or `eventDaySpan` + an inclusive-range membership test, matching FairwayAgendaView's day-mode filter at FairwayAgendaView.tsx:86-99) for each of the 7 visible days, so a multi-day event contributes a dot to every day it actually runs, matching the Month/Agenda bodies.
accessibility_check: aria-label on each day pill says '— no events' for days a multi-day event is actually running; a VoiceOver user relying on the label is told the day is free when it isn't.

user_consequence: The hero's honest status line ('N upcoming · M this week/month/in view') can under-report relative to what the body directly below it actually shows: a multi-day event that started before the visible window but is still running inside it (e.g., a Friday-start tournament viewed from the following Monday's week) is rendered by the Agenda/Month body (which correctly uses eventDaySpan overlap) but not counted in `windowCount`, which only tests whether the event's START timestamp falls inside the window.
mechanism: FairwayCalendar.tsx's `windowCount` useMemo (lines 723-751) has two branches: the `view === 'day'` branch correctly uses `eventDaySpan` overlap (matching the body), but the week/month/agenda branch (lines 743-750) filters solely on `new Date(e.start_time || e.start_date).getTime()` against `[visibleWindow.start, visibleWindow.end]` — a pure start-timestamp test with no span/overlap logic. Meanwhile the body rendered below (`FairwayAgendaView` range mode, `FairwayMonthGrid`) both use `eventDaySpan` and render the event on every day of its span that falls in the window, including when its start is before the window.
expected: Section 6 A07 order: 'Counts such as upcoming/in-view/earlier need exact set definitions' consistent with what the same screen's body displays.
actual: windowCount (in-view count) and the body's actual visible-event set use two different set definitions for week/month/agenda views (start-only vs. span-overlap); they only agree for the day view.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: define `windowCount` for every view via the same span-overlap test the day-view branch and the bodies already use (`eventDaySpan` overlap against `[visibleWindow.start, visibleWindow.end]`), not start-timestamp membership, so the header count and the rendered list are always counting the same set.

user_consequence: A player's Home 'Today' card can show the next event's time computed in the WRONG timezone whenever the team has no timezone configured (a real, already-documented state — the calendar page itself computes `teamTimezone = teamSettingsResult.data?.timezone || null`): the server render (Vercel, UTC) and the first client render (the player's own browser zone, e.g. America/New_York) can print two different times for the identical event, a ~4-5h discrepancy depending on which pass the player actually reads — the exact defect class this codebase has already found and fixed once, elsewhere.
mechanism: `src/components/fairway/pages/dashboard/player-dashboard-parts.tsx:104-114` defines its own local `formatEventTime(start, timezone?)` using `new Date(start).toLocaleTimeString('en-US', { timeZone: timezone })`. Its sole caller, `FairwayPlayerDashboard.tsx:710`, passes `timezone={enhancedData?.timezone}` — optional-chained, so it is `undefined` whenever the team timezone lookup is null. `Intl`/`toLocaleTimeString` with `timeZone: undefined` resolves to the RUNTIME's own local zone, which differs between the Vercel server process (UTC) and the browser. The canonical `formatEventTime` in `src/lib/calendar/timezone.ts:81-90` was written specifically to fix this exact class of bug (its own comment cites 'audit W1... times shift ~4h... tripped React #418') by always falling back to `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE` via `getValidTimezone` rather than the ambient runtime zone — the Home-card's local fork re-implements the same idea without that fallback, reopening the fixed defect on one surface. Confirmed as flagged independently by A04; recorded here because I own the shared calendar-timezone semantics this fork should be using.
expected: One canonical event-time formatter (src/lib/calendar/timezone.ts's formatEventTime) used everywhere an event's wall-clock time is rendered, so SSR and CSR always agree regardless of whether a team timezone is configured.
actual: A second, independent implementation exists on the player Home card with no DEFAULT_TIMEZONE fallback.
proposed_fix: SHARED CHANGE REQUEST to A04 (owns Home/player-dashboard-parts.tsx): delete the local `formatEventTime` in player-dashboard-parts.tsx and import `formatEventTime` from `@/lib/calendar/timezone` instead — same call signature (iso, timezone), already handles the null/invalid-timezone fallback correctly. I am not editing this file directly per the A04 boundary; recording the exact change here so it can land as a one-line import swap.
owner_lane: A04 (shared calendar-timezone semantics owned by A07)

user_consequence: A cross-link into the calendar for a specific event (`?event=<id>`, currently used by the Travel→Calendar 'Linked calendar event' chip) that points at an event outside the loaded/visible range, already deleted, or on the wrong team silently drops the user on the generic calendar hub with no indication their deep link resolved to nothing — no error, no toast, no 'that event isn't available' message.
mechanism: FairwayCalendar.tsx:880-887's auto-open effect only checks membership in the already-loaded `events` array (server ±3-month window plus whatever ranges the client has since fetched by navigation) — `const match = events.find((e) => e.id === initialEventId); if (!match) return;` — there is no dedicated fetch-by-id fallback for a linked event outside every range the user happens to have loaded.
expected: Section 6 A07 order: 'Deep links to missing/out-of-range events need a targeted authorized fetch or explicit unavailability, not a silent generic calendar.'
actual: A deep link to an out-of-range/deleted/wrong-team event is indistinguishable, to the user, from simply landing on the calendar with no query param at all.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: when `initialEventId` is present and not found in the loaded `events` after the initial load settles, issue one targeted `getEvent(id)`-style fetch (respecting RLS); on success, jump focus to that date and open the drawer; on a genuine miss/denial, surface an explicit 'This event is no longer available' toast/banner rather than silence.

user_consequence: An OAuth/magic-link sign-in that hits a transient golf_coaches/golf_players read failure can momentarily route an ALREADY-onboarded coach or player into first-run onboarding UI instead of the dashboard. Both onboarding pages independently self-correct (they re-check onboarding_completed on mount and redirect to /golf/dashboard), so the user does not get stuck or lose data, but they see a flash of the wrong first-run screen and pay an extra round trip - exactly the 'returning users repeat onboarding' failure the plan calls out, even though the fix elsewhere in this codebase (join/[code]/page.tsx) explicitly treats a failed identity read as fail-closed rather than fail-as-new-user.
mechanism: src/app/auth/callback/route.ts destructures only `data` from three `.single()` reads (golf_coaches, golf_players at lines 197-200; baseball_coaches/baseball_players at 231-234) and never inspects the accompanying `error`. A genuine transient read failure produces the same `{data: null}` shape as 'row does not exist', so the callback's `if (golfCoach)` / `if (golfPlayer)` checks cannot distinguish the two and fall through to 'No golf profile exists - redirect to golf signup' (line 224-227) for an existing, onboarded user.
expected: A failed profile read during OAuth callback routing should be distinguished from 'no profile exists' (same pattern already applied in src/app/golf/join/[code]/page.tsx:38-53, 100-106), and should not silently misroute an established user through onboarding UI.

user_consequence: A player with larger fingers or reduced fine-motor precision has a slightly harder time hitting the correct par (3/4/5) button per hole on the round-setup/hole-config screen than they would on any shared-primitive control elsewhere in the app, because this specific custom control is the one place that does not grow on a touch device.
mechanism: FairwayHoleConfig.tsx's per-hole par selector (lines 265-289) is a hand-rolled `<button>` (commented `eslint-disable-next-line helm/no-raw-button -- custom par-selector chip`) sized `h-9 w-9` (line 284) = 36x36 CSS-px, with `gap-1.5` (6px) between the three chips -- no overlap, but no growth path either. By contrast, the shared design-system `IconButton` (button.tsx:264) uses the SAME 36px base for its `sm` size but adds `[@media(pointer:coarse)]:h-11 [@media(pointer:coarse)]:w-11` (44px) specifically for touch devices (button.tsx:261-262's own comment: 'All sizes clear the WCAG 2.2 >=24px minimum; on coarse pointers sm expands to the DoD-preferred >=44px touch target'). Because the par chip is a custom control outside that primitive, it never receives the pointer-coarse bump and stays at 36px on every device, including touch.
expected: Per plan Section 6/A12 item 2: adopt the measured 44x44 CSS-px product touch goal for important controls, while correctly distinguishing it from the WCAG 2.5.8 AA minimum (24x24, with exceptions) so a 36px control is NOT misreported as an AA failure.
actual: 36x36 CSS-px par-selector chips PASS WCAG 2.5.8 AA (36 > 24, no exception needed) but MISS the plan's 44x44 enhanced/product goal and the pointer-coarse pattern the shared IconButton primitive already implements one file away in the same design system -- correctly framed as a P3 craft gap, not an accessibility-conformance failure.
proposed_fix: Either route the par selector through the shared IconButton/segmented-control primitive (which already has the coarse-pointer bump), or add the same `[@media(pointer:coarse)]:h-11 [@media(pointer:coarse)]:w-11` pair directly to this control's className, keeping the 6px gap so three 44px chips (150px) still fit the existing `104px` column width constraint check -- this requires re-measuring the grid template (`grid-cols-[52px_1fr_104px]`, line 257) before landing, since the par column is currently sized for 36px chips, not 44px ones.
accessibility_check: WCAG 2.5.8 AA: PASS (36px > 24px minimum, independently confirmed). WCAG 2.5.5 AAA / plan's 44px product goal: MISS.
